source.title: The two-process model of sleep regulation: a reappraisal

confidence_rationale: Canonical homeostatic-accumulator model: Process S rises monotonically as a function of prior wakefulness and falls during sleep, indexed by EEG slow-wave activity and linked to adenosine accumulation -- a homeostatic deficit variable whose antecedent is TIME-ON-TASK / metabolic expenditure, explicitly independent of aversive experience or controllability. Grounds the slow, sleep-pressure variant of fatigue/stop-recover on the SD-012 homeostatic side and supplies the recovery dynamic that suffering-withdrawal lacks. Foundational model; mapping is to the antecedent/dynamics, not a REE metric.
failure_signatures: Any account that lets a suffering/SD-011 stop signal recover by 'sleeping it off' borrows Process S dynamics it does not have: Process S recovery is specific to the homeostatic accumulator, not to aversive-uncontrollable stress.

Modelling fatigue with no recovery integrator (stop-only) omits the defining feature of Process S -- the exponential decline during sleep that resets the accumulator; fatigue without a recover phase is mis-specified.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Sleep is regulated by a homeostatic Process S and a circadian Process C. Process S increases monotonically during wakefulness and decreases during sleep; its level tracks the duration of prior wakefulness, is indexed physiologically by EEG slow-wave activity (which rises with time awake and dissipates across non-REM sleep), and is mechanistically linked to the accumulation of adenosine during waking and its clearance during sleep.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the SLOW, sleep-pressure variant of a fatigue/stop-recover signal on the SD-012 homeostatic side (and its consumer on the SD-017 sleep-timing side): a homeostatic accumulator whose antecedent is cumulative waking/effort, not aversion, and whose RECOVER phase is offline (sleep) rather than mere task-switching. This is the second, slower accumulator complementing Meyniel's within-task break accumulator -- both homeostatic, neither aversive.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Sleep biology; REE's SD-017/sleep substrate is partial and v3-pending, and REE has no adenosine homolog. The transfer is the abstract homeostatic-accumulator dynamic (monotone rise with waking, exponential reset in sleep), not the molecular substrate. Two time-constants (within-task break vs across-day sleep pressure) should not be collapsed into one variable.
mapping.source_context: Human/animal sleep EEG; reappraisal of the canonical two-process model.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, repeatedly validated model. Mapping_fidelity good for the homeostatic-accumulator dynamics and the offline-recovery half; transfer_risk moderate -- molecular substrate (adenosine) does not import, but the rise-with-waking / reset-in-sleep dynamic is the relevant, transferable abstraction for the SD-012/SD-017 fatigue variant.
